findings.description: The new re-check under the lock covers only one order: `pup fix` taking the edge before `pup land` gets the lock. In the other order the race is still open. `pup land` writes its `landed` event after it has released the merge lock and run the multi-minute audit. During that time `pup fix`'s `assertStillPinned` still sees the old merge as newest. So a fix that read the PR as OPEN before the GitHub merge passes every check under the lock, re-adds the worktree and branch that land just removed, and starts a round on a PR that has already landed.
findings.body:
**`pup fix` can still start a round on a PR that `pup land` is already landing.**

The re-check under the lock in `pup land` covers only one order: fix takes the edge first, then land gets the lock.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/38ca7e60432cbed499be6265c328fc2f0aea7585/src/core/land.service.ts#L134-L143

In the other order, fix's checks see nothing land does under the lock. Land fast-forwards, removes the worktree and deletes `pup/<id>`, then releases the lock. It writes `landed` only after the multi-minute audit:

```ts
const audit = await auditProject(db, req.repoPath, req.adapters, req.gateEnv, 'keep');
appendEvent(db, session.id, 'landed', { sha: mergeCommit, target, prUrl });
```

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/38ca7e60432cbed499be6265c328fc2f0aea7585/src/core/land.service.ts#L199-L203

Say `pup fix` read the PR as OPEN just before the GitHub merge. It then takes the merge lock, which does not block, after land releases it but before `landed` is written. Every check under fix's lock passes:
- `assertStillPinned` still finds the old `merge` event as the newest, at the pinned sha.
- `restoreWorktree` finds no branch, so `worktree add -b` re-creates `pup/<id>` and the worktree at the head.
- `takeFixRoundEdge` succeeds, because the row is still `merged`.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/38ca7e60432cbed499be6265c328fc2f0aea7585/src/core/fix-round.service.ts#L144-L148
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/38ca7e60432cbed499be6265c328fc2f0aea7585/src/core/fix-round.service.ts#L398-L411

The worker is relaunched on a landed PR, with the branch and worktree that land just removed. `landed` is then appended after `fix_round`, so the session is `running` while its newest merge reads `'landed'`. `assertStillPinned`'s docstring says it covers "a `pup land` that finished while the review was read", which holds only once the audit is done.

The window is narrow: the time between fix's read and its lock has to cover the merge click and land's locked section. It can happen when the conductor lands while the operator runs `pup fix`.

Possible fixes:
- Give fix something land changes under the lock. For example, under fix's lock, refuse when the pinned sha is already an ancestor of `refs/remotes/origin/<target>`, which land updates under the lock.
- Or record `landed`, or a landing marker, inside land's lock before `tearDown`.

findings.description: When threads come with no status, or with the poster's 'the review could not be posted' FAILURE, or the run died before its `finally`, the refusal says to wait, but waiting never clears those states; only an `@claude review` comment re-runs the head, and only PENDING gets that hint.

The final-status gate does not bind the threads to the run that set the status: the poster's status write is best-effort and its review carries no `commit_id`, so an earlier run's threads can sit beside a later run's no-verdict FAILURE, or an older final status can survive a re-run whose status write failed, on the same head. Requiring `status.state === 'SUCCESS'` narrows this; decision 90's 'same run' claim overstates it.

A `pup kill` during the kickoff wait moves the row to merged; `undoRound`'s `killSession` then tries merged → killed and throws InvalidTransitionError, masking the original error and skipping the worktree `rmSync`/prune (the old undo threw too, but now the worktree is also left).

`killedFixRoundMessage` puts the store-read session id unsanitised into an `rm -r .worktrees/<id>` command (reached from `pup ui`'s kill with no `assertMintedRow`), while the matching `restoreWorktree` refusal sanitises it; a forged row id like `s ~` yields a destructive command if pasted. Name the command only for a `SESSION_ID_PATTERN` id, and share one cleanup-instruction string between the two sites.

`relaunchWorker` re-implements `startSession`'s post-compile steps (`writeCompiledProfile`, then the `prepareGraph(binary, …) ? join(compiledDir, 'mcp.json') : undefined` ternary, now its third copy), and the unnamed `{ compiled: CompiledProfile; binary: string | undefined }` pair is spelled out three times; one session-lifecycle helper that writes the profile and returns the settings/mcp paths would serve both.

`ProfileSource` includes `role`, but the launch stores only the role's name and `pup fix` never passes one, so the type suggests a faithful recompile it cannot give; drop `role` from it or resolve it from the task row.

`recompileSessionProfile` turns scope conflicts into kickoff peers but never calls `introduceToPeers` or writes a `scope_overlap` event as `launchTask` does, so live peers sharing files are not told the round's worker is editing again.
Threads are relayed under a `partial review: …` SUCCESS status while the clean path requires the exact full-review string; probably intended, but the asymmetry is undocumented in decision 90.

In decision 90, the inserted sentence about `pup merge` printing `rejection 1/2` now sits before "That event, carrying the thread ids…", so "That event" no longer points at the `fix_round` event; move the insertion or name the event.

Decision 90 says "three commands that would lose the round refuse" but lists two refusals (respawn/`kill --respawn`, plain merge) and then `pup land`'s re-check, which is not a refusal of that kind; reword as two refusals and one re-check.

Decision 90's Tests paragraph narrates review history ("Round 2 of CI review added…") rather than what the tests cover, and several edited lines (that one, the `Default_Ignorable_Code_Point` sentence, the decision 83 note) wrap unevenly.

The `relaunchWorker` JSDoc has one overlong line ("a round, back to `merged`, and its worktree removed, so `pup fix` can be re-run; the `fix_round` event") followed by a short one; reflow the paragraph.

`compileSessionProfile`'s JSDoc "Compile a session's profile into its compiled dir's path, not yet written" is garbled, and the function does `mkdirSync` the dir; e.g. "Compile a session's profile for its compiled dir without writing the files."

`ReviewThread.isMinimized`'s JSDoc ("as an injection attempt is hidden") is speculative and inexact, since the flag is true for anything but a plain `false`; state that contract and drop the inline comment that repeats it.
The land refusal renders `moved to gone` when the row is missing (`now ?? 'gone'`), and the `CiReview` JSDoc's "which is what the status says, never proof" reads clumsily; reword both.

`let delivered = false;` (and `edited` in github.client.ts:425) are booleans left without an is/has prefix next to the delta's `hasRowMoved`/`isEditedByOther` renames (docs/conventions/general.md §Type safety).
